FR-003.title: Loading the parser component MUST be triggered by use, never by import, so that a future installation that renames or relocates it degrades to "parser unavailable" instead of break

FR-004.title: Before use, the system MUST verify that the parser component comes from the same installation directory as the data model in use, and MUST refuse otherwise.

FR-005.title: Before use, the system MUST verify by inspection that every operation it intends to call exists, and MUST bind those operations positionally rather than by parameter name.

FR-006.title: The detected parser version MUST be reported and MUST NOT be compared against any minimum. A standing test MUST guard this in each repository that probes.

FR-007.title: Scripts MUST be able to read all genres assigned to a text, not only the first.

FR-008.title: Scripts MUST be able to get the entry that owns an allomorph.

FR-009.title: Scripts MUST be able to read morpho-syntactic analyses without dropping to raw data-model access, since resolving a user's hypothesis terminates in them.

FR-010.title: Parser results crossing into script-visible form MUST preserve the identity of the underlying lexical objects, not only their text, because later checkpoints align results against

FR-012.title: The assistant MUST offer a tool that parses one word and MUST expose all three levels of answer: restricted-to-a-hypothesis, plain yes/no, and full explanation. Each MUST reach the

FR-013.title: The plain yes/no level MUST NOT present itself as explaining a failure, and MUST point the caller at an explaining level instead.

FR-014.title: Guidance MUST steer callers to the restricted level when they have a hypothesis and to the full explanation only when they do not, since the full explanation is the expensive one a

FR-015.title: Every handler that reaches the parser MUST check the project's configured parser engine as its first action, before any parser is constructed, and MUST refuse a project configured

FR-016.title: A missing recording agent MUST NOT mark reading unavailable, since reading neither records nor needs one.

FR-017.title: The new tools MUST be annotated read-only-safe, and that annotation MUST be backed by a standing test asserting that a real parse loads no user-interface framework code into the pr

FR-018.title: The restricted trace MUST accept a decomposition expressed in terms a caller can actually write -- entry headwords, headword plus sense, or internal identifiers -- and resolve it t

FR-019.title: If any piece of a decomposition resolves to no usable analysis, the request MUST be refused, naming the piece, its position and its candidates, and no parse MUST be run.

FR-020.title: Lookup structures used for resolution MUST be built once per run and reused across words.

FR-021.title: Where every piece has exactly one unambiguous candidate, the system MAY offer a proposed decomposition; when it does, it MUST label it proposed and unverified.

FR-022.title: Guidance offered when a decomposition is missing MUST name only actions the caller can actually perform with the tools that exist.

FR-023.title: A caller's proposed decomposition MUST always be traced exactly as given. The system MUST NOT substitute a different restriction, widen it to an unrestricted search, reorder, score

FR-024.title: Where the system has something to say about a proposal, it MUST be limited to an adjacent candidate or a conflict with recorded analyses, MUST be worded as an observation rather th

FR-025.title: Agreement between a proposal and recorded analyses MUST produce no commentary.

FR-026.title: All parser execution MUST go through one run mechanism. There MUST NOT be a separate synchronous path.

FR-027.title: A run MUST report a distinct stage for starting, loading the grammar, parsing, filing (defined but unreachable in this checkpoint), completed, failed and cancelled.

FR-028.title: A run reaching a terminal stage inside a configurable grace window (default 5 seconds) MUST return its results inline; otherwise it MUST return a handle. The window governs reporti

FR-029.title: Results MUST be written to the run's record as they are produced, so a run that dies or is cancelled leaves everything completed so far readable.

FR-030.title: Runs MUST be ordered by the same priority levels and ordering the host application uses, lowest value first, first-in-first-out within a level, enqueued per word.

FR-031.title: A higher-priority single word MUST interleave at the running batch's next word boundary. The batch MUST NOT restart or lose position, the grammar MUST NOT be reloaded, and the batc

FR-032.title: Cancellation MUST be cooperative, stopping at the next word boundary and leaving a cancelled terminal stage over the partial results.

FR-033.title: The assistant MUST offer a read-only status tool taking a run handle and reporting stage, progress, and -- on a terminal stage -- the result summary or the failure with its guidanc

FR-034.title: A failed run MUST carry guidance pointing at the diagnostic instruments, since memory exhaustion is the case where a diagnosis beats a retry.

FR-035.title: A status request for an unknown handle MUST be refused naming the handle and the handles that do exist.

FR-036.title: A cancelled run MUST be reportable with the count of words completed and the stage it was in when cancelled.

FR-038.title: Every piece of guidance shipped in CP1 that had to point at nothing because this tool did not exist MUST be revisited and pointed at it.

FR-039.title: Test groups deferred by CP1 MUST be brought into scope: the no-user-interface-code guarantee, the no-oracle case, the conditional-proposal case, and the script-library facade group

FR-040.title: Whether the three grammar lints deferred at CP1 are folded in here MUST be decided and, if deferred again, recorded as such.
